**Bizum, Bancomat, Wero and peers form joint entity for pan-European payments**

*Five domestic payment schemes have created a shared company in Madrid to build cross-border interoperability, marking the most concrete step yet in Europe's push to reduce dependence on US card networks.*

Bizum, Bancomat, Wero (the European Payments Initiative's consumer-facing brand), Portugal's SIBS-MB WAY and Norway's Vipps MobilePay have established a joint entity to connect their networks into a single cross-continent payments infrastructure. The new company, based in Madrid, is designed to let consumers and merchants use their domestic payment methods seamlessly across participating European markets.

The initiative moves beyond the memoranda of understanding and pilot phases that have characterised previous European sovereignty efforts. By incorporating a legal entity with shared governance, the five schemes are committing operational and financial resources to interoperability rather than simply signalling intent. The group collectively covers consumers in Spain, Italy, Germany, France, the Benelux, Portugal and the Nordics.

For Visa and Mastercard, the competitive threat is still distant but increasingly structured. The new entity sits alongside rather than replaces the individual schemes, meaning each retains its domestic brand and user base. The question is whether a federated model can deliver the network effects and merchant acceptance that the US duopoly has built over decades. For European policymakers who have urged payment sovereignty since at least 2020, this is the clearest market-led response to date.

*Sources: [European payments groups join forces in challenge to US](https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2026/1001/1593639-european-payments-group/) — RTE | [European payments partners form new entity to expand interoperability](https://www.electronicpaymentsinternational.com/news/european-payments-partners-form-new-entity-to-expand-interoperability/) — Electronicpaymentsinternational | [European payments groups join forces to take on US giants](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48517/european-payments-groups-join-forces-to-take-on-us-giants?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Zilch engages banks for potential London IPO in 2027**

*A potential London listing would test appetite for fintech IPOs on the exchange after Wise's departure and Klarna's mixed New York reception, with the open banking-native BNPL provider reportedly sounding out investment banks.*

Zilch, the UK-based buy-now-pay-later firm that uses open banking APIs for real-time affordability checks rather than traditional credit scoring, has engaged banks to explore a London IPO targeted for 2027. The company is understood to be in early-stage conversations about listing structure and timing.

Zilch's model is unusual in the BNPL sector. It connects directly to customers' bank accounts via open banking to assess affordability at the point of transaction, positioning it closer to an open banking payments company than a conventional credit provider. A London listing would test appetite for fintech IPOs on the exchange after Wise moved its primary listing to the US in February and Klarna's New York debut produced a cautious market response.

Zilch's reliance on open banking data for underwriting could prove a differentiator under the FCA's new BNPL regulatory framework, which took effect on July 15. The regime requires lenders to demonstrate robust affordability assessments, a standard Zilch's model is already designed to meet.

*Sources: [Zilch reportedly engages banks for potential London IPO](https://www.fintechfutures.com/stock-exchange-ipos/zilch-reportedly-engages-banks-for-london-ipo) — FinTech Futures | [Zilch Lines Up Bankers for 2027 London IPO Amid Post-Klarna Market Caution](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/328345/20260930/zilch-lines-bankers-2027-london-ipo-amid-post-klarna-market-caution.htm) — Tech Times*

**Verification of payee requirements diverge as US plans lag behind Europe**

*Europe's regulatory mandate for payee verification is pulling ahead of voluntary US approaches, with implications for fraud prevention and cross-border payment interoperability.*

Europe's Instant Payments Regulation requires payment service providers to verify that a payee's name matches the account identifier before completing a transfer. In the US, payee verification remains largely voluntary and fragmented, with no federal mandate equivalent to the European framework. PYMNTS reports that while US industry groups are developing plans, the absence of regulatory compulsion has left adoption patchy.

As instant payment corridors multiply between jurisdictions, inconsistent verification standards create weak points that fraudsters can exploit. Europe's approach, which builds on earlier schemes such as the Netherlands' SurePay and the UK's Confirmation of Payee, embeds verification as a compliance requirement rather than a competitive feature.

Payments routed through US rails lack the same pre-transaction checks, meaning fraud risk is asymmetric across the Atlantic. The European model is not without its own implementation challenges, as earlier reporting on verification of payee delays has shown, but the regulatory direction is clear. The US remains in a consultative phase with no firm timeline.

*Sources: [Europe's Payee Checks Set the Pace as US Plans Take Shape](https://www.pymnts.com/news/cross-border-payments/2026/europe-payee-checks-set-pace-united-states-plans-take-shape/) — PYMNTS.com*

**Payments Association acquires European counterpart to build cross-border advocacy**

*The acquisition of TPA-EU creates a combined lobbying and standards organisation spanning UK and EU payments policy, at a moment when regulatory frameworks on both sides are in flux.*

The Payments Association, the UK's principal payments trade body, has acquired its European counterpart, the Third Party Payments Association EU (TPA-EU). The combined organisation will operate across both UK and EU jurisdictions, giving members a single point of engagement on regulatory and policy matters that increasingly require coordination across the two regimes.

The deal comes as the UK consults on modernising its payments regulatory framework, including the proposed merger of the Payment Systems Regulator (PSR) into the FCA, while the EU is finalising the Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3) and the Payment Services Regulation. For firms operating in both markets, navigating two diverging but related regulatory tracks has become a significant compliance burden. A combined trade body may offer more coherent industry input into both processes.

The Payments Association currently coordinates with the Bank of England, the FCA, the Treasury, the PSR, Pay.UK, UK Finance and Innovate Finance. Adding TPA-EU's relationships with European institutions and national regulators gives the merged entity a broader remit at a time when cross-border alignment on issues such as open banking standards, fraud prevention and instant payments interoperability remains incomplete.

*Sources: [UK: The Payments Association Acquires European Counterpart TPA-EU](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2026/10/314780-uk-the-payments-association-acquires-european-counterpart-tpa-eu/) — Crowdfund Insider*
